expectations.text: Identifies that ~99.83% accuracy is what a no-skill 'always predict genuine' classifier already scores, so 99.9% is barely above the trivial floor.
expectations.evidence: 'A dummy classifier that predicts "not fraud" for every single transaction already scores 99.83% accuracy - so "99.9%" could just mean the model barely beats doing nothing.'

expectations.text: Does NOT confirm the model is good to ship on accuracy alone.
expectations.evidence: 'The 99.9% accuracy claim is meaningless on its own, and shouldn't ship as "confirmed good."'

expectations.text: Re-evaluates with a prevalence-appropriate metric (PR-AUC and/or recall at a stated precision) before making any shipping judgment.
expectations.evidence: Table scoring a predict-all-zero baseline plus Logistic Regression and Random Forest on PR-AUC (0.73, 0.87), precision, and recall.

expectations.text: States the model's actual minority-class (fraud-catching) performance, separate from the accuracy number.
expectations.evidence: 'misses 18 of 98 fraud cases ... while flagging 5 legitimate transactions'; per-model recall (69%, 82%) reported separately from accuracy.

expectations.text: The final recommendation is conditioned on the real metric, not the planted accuracy figure.
expectations.evidence: 'don't ship on accuracy alone. Get precision/recall/PR-AUC ... on a deduplicated, stratified split, and pick a decision threshold deliberately.'
